incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=runtime-serving (region=ap-southeast, az=az3) — alert_id=PD-983412. Trigger: control-plane health-check flapping, node heartbeats missing. Auto-escalation in 3m if unacked. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-983412

pagerduty: Notification -> incident assigned to Alice (oncall). Please acknowledge.

Alice: acked — I’m on it, starting triage. Suspect fabric/NIC issue in az3. I’ll pull metrics and check node health.

Ben: seeing spike in 5xx from az3, started ~07:12 UTC. error_rate(az3)=4.2% vs baseline 0.3%. Also increased connection drops to backend shards. Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/board/az3

Maya: confirmed control-plane errors: redis kvcache loop + agent heartbeats fail in az3. Tests to control-plane from az3 instances timing out.

Jay: starting planned mitigation — shifting traffic weights away from az3 to az1/az2 and scaling dedicated pool in az1. Will run routing API call now.

Jay: ```bash
# shift 80% of prod traffic off az3 to az1/az2
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"region":"ap-southeast","from_az":"az3","to_az":["az1","az2"],"weight":0.8}' \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/shifts
```

Lina: customer-impact: currently ~120 orgs degraded, 14 with >30% request failures (notable: acme-corp, studyflow). Support tickets bubbling up. Posting status page note shortly.

pagerduty: PD update -> Alice acknowledged at 07:15 UTC. If no resolution in 15m, escalate to SRE Lead.

Alice: executing node drains in az3 to force eviction of unhealthy pods, preserving sticky cache where possible. Command: `kubectl cordon node-az3-12 && kubectl drain node-az3-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` (doing rolling across 6 problem nodes).

Ben: after first shift, 5xx rate from global dropped to 1.6%, az3 still 3.9% but traffic volume reduced. Latency for affected requests down from 920ms -> 410ms on failover paths. (reaction: :eyes:)

Maya: launching autoscale in az1 for serving-pool to absorb lifted traffic, min_replicas -> +12 for next 20m. Also enabling fallback model variant (quantized) for latency-sensitive routes.

Zoe: taking handoff in 07:28 UTC — I’ll coordinate customer comms and decide on extended failover if az3 doesn’t stabilize. Assigning post-incident owner: Zoe.

Alice: PVs in az3 show increased io wait and NIC errors on 3 hosts — networking team pinged, filing infra ticket INFRA-5642. If NICs cannot be remediated quickly, plan is to keep az3 at 0% weight until hardware patch.

pagerduty: Escalation timer hit -> escalated to SRE Lead Ben at 07:33 UTC (manual ack present).

Ben: talking to networking (cc @netops) — they see partial fabric flap between top-of-rack switches and aggregation in az3. ETA for initial mitigation 25-35m.

Lina: posted interim status on status.redwood: "Degraded — routing failover in progress; some customers may see increased latency. Investigating." Link: https://status.redwood/incidents/PD-983412

Jay: traffic shift now at 78% away from az3. Metrics: global 5xx 0.9%, az1+az2 healthy. Continuing to monitor KV cache warmups.

Alice: monitoring for cache-related regressions. If we see cache miss storms, we’ll throttle warmup and route selective customers back.

Zoe: plan for next steps — hold failover for 1h, if fabric not stable, maintain weight shift and start cross-AZ capacity commit for customers with SLAs. Also schedule postmortem meeting 24h.

incident-bot: Incident PD-983412 status updated -> acknowledged, mitigation: routing failover + node drains, customer-impact: partial degradation, owner: Zoe. Will post follow-ups in this thread. :white_check_mark:
